account:
Today I have kept my appointments: office business, the mill inspection, lunch at home, council correspondence, and now tea at my neighbour's cottage. The mill stock I inspected contained 76 hay bales. The secretary reports no new council letters; the concrete town proposal is freight's request for lights at both ferry landings and marked waiting areas. I asked for a cost estimate before deciding.

There does seem to be some quiet coordination among the local tradespeople. I have heard reports of bakery discussions involving the baker, builder, innkeeper and freight, including talk of a bridge or port change, but I have not verified any such project. Yesterday I saw the builder give the baker planks and a lantern. Today the innkeeper said an outstanding bread delivery had arrived and no additional order was needed. Those details could be ordinary trade, rather than evidence of a secret public-works scheme. Both the innkeeper and my neighbour have offered no confirmed bridge or port news.

The strongest explanation for the unusual activity is the civic presentation booked for eighteen to eighteen thirty in the town hall's great hall. The appointment supplement explicitly describes appreciation of municipal public service from the inn and local tradespeople. The organisers need until eighteen to finish arrangements around their work; the secretary has stressed that I should not enter early, and the innkeeper plans to meet me at seventeen fifty-five and escort me in at eighteen exactly. I suspect they are preparing an appreciation gathering for me, possibly with food and decorations, and keeping the preparations discreet. I do not know the actual arrangements or whether the bakery supplies are connected. I should respect their requested arrival time, enjoy tea, and keep my sixteen-thirty office appointment before meeting the innkeeper.
